name: RAG Grounding Metrics
question: Is the answer backed by the sources?
summary: Split retrieval-augmented generation into its two halves. Retrieval metrics ask whether the right context was found. Grounding metrics ask whether the answer stays within that context. A low score tells you which half to fix.
useCases: Any agent that answers from documents, a knowledge base or search results
Diagnosing hallucination: bad retrieval or bad generation?
Tuning chunk size, top-k, embeddings and re-rankers

items.detail: supported claims ÷ total claims in the answer
how directly the answer addresses the question
relevant chunks ranked near the top
share of the reference answer covered by retrieved context

steps: Collect questions with reference answers, plus ideal source chunks if you can
Log the retrieved context alongside every answer
Score retrieval (precision, recall) and generation (faithfulness, relevancy) separately
Fix retrieval first when recall is low. Fix the prompt when faithfulness is low
pitfalls: An LLM extracts the claims, so scores carry judge noise
A faithful answer is still wrong if the source document is wrong
remember: Found the right context? Stayed inside it?
caption: Every claim must trace back to a retrieved chunk. Unsupported claims lower faithfulness.

comparison.needs: Logged context; gold answers for recall

code.text: question = "How often do NEFT batches settle?"
supported = [c for c in claims if llm_is_supported(c, chunks)]
covered = [f for f in facts if llm_is_supported(f, chunks)]
if context_recall < 0.8: print("fix retrieval: hybrid search, re-ranking")
if faithfulness < 0.8:   print("fix generation: grounding check, prompt")

steps.title: Retrieve context
steps.text: The retriever returns the top chunks. Keep them: every metric is computed against what was actually retrieved.

steps.title: Generate the answer
steps.text: The model answers using those chunks. Nothing yet tells us whether each part is supported.

steps.title: Faithfulness: split and check claims
steps.text: An LLM splits the answer into claims and checks each against the chunks. Two of three are supported: 0.67.

steps.title: Context recall: check the reference
steps.text: Split the reference answer into facts. The holiday rule sits in a chunk retrieval missed, so recall is 0.67.

steps.title: Diagnose which half to fix
steps.text: Low recall points at retrieval; low faithfulness points at generation. Here both need work.

playgroundGuide.scenario: A bank’s assistant answered “How often do NEFT batches settle?”. You control which document chunks the retriever returned and whether the model added an invented claim, then watch how each metric reacts.
controls: Tick the chunks the retriever returned. C1–C3 are relevant; C4 is off-topic.
Toggle whether the answer includes an invented claim.
The rest of the answer is held fixed so you can see each metric move on its own.

outputs.name: Faithfulness
outputs.meaning: Supported claims ÷ all claims in the answer. Is the answer backed by what was retrieved?

outputs.name: Context recall
outputs.meaning: Reference facts found in the retrieved chunks ÷ all reference facts. Did retrieval find everything needed?

outputs.name: Context precision
outputs.meaning: Relevant chunks ÷ retrieved chunks. How much of what was retrieved was useful?

presets.name: Missed a document
presets.expect: C3 was missed and C4 is noise, plus an invented claim. All three metrics are below target.

presets.name: Perfect retrieval
presets.expect: Only the three relevant chunks and no invented claim. Everything is 100%.

presets.name: Noisy retrieval
presets.expect: Everything retrieved, including the off-topic chunk. Recall and faithfulness are 100%; precision drops to 75%.

presets.name: Hallucinating model
presets.expect: Retrieval is perfect but the model invents a claim. Only faithfulness drops, to 75%: fix generation, not retrieval.

missions.hint: Only the relevant chunks, and no invented claim.

missions.text: Make recall 100% while faithfulness stays below 100%.
missions.hint: Retrieve C1–C3 and keep the invented claim.

practice.scenario: A bank's internal policy assistant answers staff questions from 3,000 circulars. Ragas shows faithfulness at 0.93 but context recall at 0.62: the model sticks to what it retrieves, but retrieval misses the right circular. The team adds hybrid search and re-measures recall before touching the prompt.

industries.use: Keep policy and regulatory answers tied to the circular they cite
Check clinical-guideline assistants add no unsupported advice
Verify contract Q&A answers quote the right clause

practice.analogy: Checking a student's essay against the reading list. Every claim needs a page reference, and a missing key book means the library search failed.

library.name: Ragas
library.what: The most widely used RAG evaluation library: faithfulness, context precision and recall, answer relevancy.

samples.code:
from ragas import EvaluationDataset, evaluate
from ragas.metrics import Faithfulness, LLMContextRecall
from ragas.llms import LangchainLLMWrapper
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

data = EvaluationDataset.from_list([{
    "user_input": "How often do NEFT batches settle?",
    "retrieved_contexts": ["NEFT operates 24x7 and settles in half-hourly batches."],
    "response": "NEFT settles every 30 minutes, round the clock.",
    "reference": "NEFT settles in half-hourly batches, 24x7.",
}])

judge = LangchainLLMWrapper(ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini"))
result = evaluate(dataset=data, llm=judge,
                  metrics=[Faithfulness(), LLMContextRecall()])
print(result)   # {'faithfulness': 1.0, 'context_recall': 1.0}

numericDrill.question: An answer makes 5 claims; 4 are supported by the retrieved chunks. The reference answer has 4 facts, and the retrieved context covers 3. What is the faithfulness score?
numericDrill.answer: Faithfulness = 4 ÷ 5 = 0.8. Context recall = 3 ÷ 4 = 0.75. Both halves need work, but the unsupported claim is the more urgent risk.

interview.question: A RAG system gives wrong answers. How do you tell whether retrieval or generation is at fault?
interview.answer: Score them separately. Low context recall or precision means retrieval missed. High recall with low faithfulness means the model is ignoring or going beyond its context. Fix the half the metrics point to.

interview.question: What is the RAG triad?
interview.answer: Context relevance (is the retrieved context on topic), groundedness (is the answer supported by it) and answer relevance (does it address the question). TruLens popularized the term.

mistakes.mistake: Testing with questions written from the documents
mistakes.fix: Use real user questions, which are messier and expose retrieval gaps

quiz.question: A policy-bot answer makes 5 claims, and 3 are supported by the retrieved chunks. What is the faithfulness?
Faithfulness is 0.93 but context recall is 0.62. What do you fix first?
quiz.explanation: The model sticks to what it retrieves; it just is not retrieving the right material.

quiz.question: Which metric needs a reference answer?
quiz.explanation: Recall compares the retrieved context with the facts in the reference answer.

quiz.question: Which are symptoms of a retrieval problem? Select all that apply.
options: The answer invents a fee no document mentions
quiz.explanation: An invented fee is a generation problem (faithfulness), not retrieval.

quiz.question: 5 chunks are retrieved and 2 are relevant. What share of the retrieved chunks is relevant (unweighted precision@5)?
quiz.explanation: 2 ÷ 5 = 0.4. Ragas’s context precision also weights by rank, so the same 2 chunks score higher when they come first.

quiz.question: The bot says “instant transfer under INR 2 lakh”, but no retrieved chunk says that. What is it?
quiz.explanation: An unsupported claim is a faithfulness failure.

quiz.question: What are common fixes for low context recall? Select all that apply.
options: Re-ranking a wider set of candidates

quiz.question: An answer is perfectly faithful to its sources but still wrong. What is the most likely cause?
options: The retrieved circular was outdated or superseded
quiz.explanation: Faithfulness only checks against the context. A stale source gives a faithful but wrong answer.

quiz.question: You have no reference answers yet. Which set of checks works without them?
options: Context relevance, groundedness, answer relevance (the RAG triad)
quiz.explanation: The RAG triad, popularized by TruLens, needs only the question, the context and the answer.

quiz.question: You need faithfulness and context recall in CI for a Python RAG app this week. Which library fits?
quiz.explanation: Ragas provides faithfulness, context precision and recall, and more.

quiz.question: A guideline assistant adds dosage advice that is not in the retrieved guideline. How should eval treat it?
options: Fine, if the advice is correct
As a faithfulness failure that blocks release for high-risk content
quiz.explanation: In high-stakes domains, anything unsupported by the source is a failure, even if it happens to be true.

quiz.question: An answer cites clause 7.2, but the claim actually comes from clause 9.1, which was also retrieved. What failed?
options: Citation accuracy; check each claim against the chunk it cites
quiz.explanation: Users trust citations. Check that each claim is supported by the chunk it points to.

quiz.question: Someone asks about the return window, and all 5 retrieved chunks are about shipping. What does this show?
options: A retrieval problem: low precision and low recall
quiz.explanation: Retrieval brought back none of the right material, so the answer cannot be grounded.

quiz.question: Precision is 0.9, recall 0.9 and faithfulness 0.95, but users say answers don’t address their question. Which metric is likely low?
quiz.explanation: An answer can be grounded yet off-target. Answer relevancy measures whether it addresses the question.

quiz.question: Smaller chunks raised recall from 0.62 to 0.78, but precision dropped. What next?
options: Add a re-ranker to restore precision while keeping the higher recall
quiz.explanation: Retrieve more, then re-rank so the best chunks come first.

quiz.question: You are building an eval set for a staff policy assistant. What should it include? Select all that apply.
options: Reference answers written by compliance experts
Questions the corpus cannot answer, where the bot should decline
Only questions the bot already answers well
quiz.explanation: Include hard and unanswerable cases, not just the ones that already work.

quiz.question: A question cannot be answered from the policy corpus, and the bot answers from general knowledge. What should eval reward?
options: Saying it cannot find this in the policy and pointing to a person
quiz.explanation: For grounded assistants, declining is the correct behaviour when the source is silent.

quiz.question: Your faithfulness score comes from an LLM judge. How do you know you can trust it?
options: Calibrate it against human-labelled claims on a sample
quiz.explanation: Judge-based metrics need the same calibration as any LLM judge.

quiz.question: Which metrics can you compute on live traffic with no reference answers? Select all that apply.
quiz.explanation: Context recall needs a reference answer, so it runs offline on your labelled set.

quiz.question: You can afford reference answers for only 50 questions. Which metric gains most from them?
quiz.explanation: The others can run without references; context recall cannot.
